ci_evidence.name: KM1 Application Foundation and KM2 Pilot — PostgreSQL 16 migrations, 23 application/pilot tests, CLI help, Compose config and Docker image build
AI Reviewer Evidence before the report-only commit

findings.finding: The example publisher trust policy is a template. Its signer public-key fingerprint and source commit are intentionally placeholders; local package admission is denied until an operator pins the real values in an ignored local file. The trust-policy file itself is a local operator-controlled input, not a separately signed policy service.
findings.disposition: Do not publish or install a package from the template unchanged. For hosted environments, store and version the policy through an administrator-controlled configuration/KMS/secret-management mechanism and add policy-change approval/audit.

findings.finding: The pilot intentionally supports only the built-in hsmart.echo.v1 entrypoint. Package payloads are not imported or executed. This is safe for a controlled first-party pilot but is not a general-purpose plugin runtime or sandbox.
findings.disposition: Do not admit third-party plugin entrypoints. Before general execution, design isolated workloads, resource limits, network/filesystem policy, image provenance, tenant isolation, kill/timeout and cleanup controls.

findings.finding: The local integration uses a generated test Ed25519 key and a PEM verification key path. The hosted code path requires an HTTPS JWKS URL, but production issuer/client registration, JWKS rotation, workload identity and KMS/HSM signer custody are not provisioned or tested.
findings.disposition: Keep local test keys out of production. Provision an externally managed OIDC issuer/client, asymmetric key rotation and KMS/HSM-backed publisher signing before hosted activation.

findings.finding: The audit chain is hash-linked and verified in tests, and tenant sequence allocation uses a PostgreSQL tenant-row lock. Audit rows remain in the application database; this is not an independently protected WORM/object-lock store. No production telemetry pipeline or alerting/SLO is deployed.
findings.disposition: Add an external append-only/WORM audit sink, independent integrity checkpointing, trace/metric export, alerts and retention/restore tests before production.

findings.finding: Docker Compose and a container image are validated in CI, but no cloud provider, region, public domain, ingress/TLS, managed PostgreSQL, managed Redis, object store, backup policy, restore test or DR/failover exercise has been provisioned.
findings.disposition: Retain LOCAL_PILOT_ONLY. Hosted staging requires GOV-01 vendor/region/domain/identity/cost decisions; production requires backup/restore and DR proof.

findings.finding: The sample trust policy authorizes only the first-party HSMART Echo package under the HSMART repository LICENSE and an explicit source-commit allowlist. It does not grant rights to any Hypersystem plugin, private Plugin Creator package or upstream dependency.
findings.disposition: Keep all wider USER/PRIVATE packages blocked from registry distribution until canonical source, publisher authorization, license/NOTICE attribution, third-party rights and package integrity are individually accepted.

findings.finding: The local pilot does not yet implement production rate/quotas, admin separation of duties, policy approvals, external malware scanning/SBOM/attestation pipeline, automated signer rotation or operator alert/runbook drills.
findings.disposition: Treat as staged production gates; do not infer these capabilities from the signed-package or CI implementation.

Select and authorize cloud provider, region, domain/DNS/TLS, OIDC tenant/client and budget; none is provisioned by this PR.
Create/authorize canonical child repositories and approve a per-package redistribution/license decision; HSMART trust policy is limited to its own first-party sample.
Separate sandbox/runtime, managed identity/key custody, WORM audit, monitoring, backup/restore, DR, security and production acceptance evidence.

limitations: This is a correlation-limited AI assurance review, not independent provider/model certification.
GOV-11 is a logical designation and has not been provisioned as an isolated reviewer runtime.
The same assistant conversation participated in implementation and review; native GitHub approval is false.
CI proves the named migrations/tests and build on the exact reviewed head only; it does not prove hosted or production deployment.
MCP proof is a local stdio subprocess integration test, not remote MCP/HTTP Gateway deployment or an external host integration.
The package verifier accepts only first-party built-in entrypoints; arbitrary uploaded code is deliberately out of scope.
The trust-policy template must be populated locally with exact signer/source values before a local package can be built/installed.
No third-party USER/PRIVATE plugin package is authorized by the sample publisher policy.
disposition: The reviewed change set is acceptable with caveats as a KM2 local signed-registry, installer, entitlement and stdio MCP pilot foundation. Exact-head PostgreSQL/application tests, cross-platform specification tests, repository governance, CLI checks, Compose validation and Docker image build passed. The pilot must remain LOCAL_PILOT_ONLY; public cloud, production runtime, arbitrary package execution and third-party plugin distribution are not authorized by this evidence. GOV-01 retains final merge and risk-acceptance authority.
